extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III, the provider may generally choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except that where the system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions, the relevant market surveillance authority shall act as the notified body.

Annex VII third-party notified body assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems, whereas most other high-risk AI systems may use the Annex VI self-assessment (internal control) route.

For high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products already covered by Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral EU conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements.

A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, unless the modification is a predetermined change in a system designed to continue learning after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to derogate from the standard conformity assessment procedure (Article 43) for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life/health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Under Annex VII point 4.5, where other means of verifying conformity with Chapter III Section 2 requirements have proven insufficient, a notified body may, upon reasoned request, be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 governs the assignment of identification numbers and the publication of lists of notified bodies designated under the AI Act.

The 2021 and 2022 Commission/Council proposal drafts of Article 43 required that for Annex III point 1 (biometric) systems, where harmonised standards or common specifications were applied, the provider had to follow one of a set of listed conformity assessment procedures — language that differs from the final adopted text.

As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem specifically for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and limited capacity, ahead of an August 2026 deadline for high-risk obligations.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the medical devices/SaMD context.
High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act, including conformity assessment requirements, are generally described as becoming fully applicable in August 2026.

A Council document (7322/26) sets out a coding system (e.g., AIP 0101, AIP 0102) under Article 30 for defining the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified for categories of AI systems listed in Annex I of the AI Act.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would create a new Annex XIV listing AI Act-related categories for the Commission's NANDO notified-body database and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements, but this is a proposal, not yet adopted law.

As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 notified bodies designated under the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR); these are existing sectoral designations, not AI Act-specific designations.

The Commission publishes designated notified bodies in the NANDO information system, filterable by legislation, as part of the general EU approach to notified body oversight (illustrated via MDR/IVDR practice).

Under the separate Cyber Resilience Act (CRA, not the AI Act), as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO, with a target of sufficient notified body capacity by 11 December 2026 and full application from 11 December 2027.

contradictions.claim_a: The 2021/2022 proposal versions of Article 43 state that for Annex III point 1 (biometric) high-risk systems, where harmonised standards or common specifications are applied, the provider 'shall follow one of the following procedures' (i.e., a conditional set of options tied to standards).
contradictions.claim_b: The final/current AI Act Service Desk text of Article 43 states the provider 'may choose any of the notified bodies,' with a specific carve-out only for law enforcement/immigration/asylum/Union-institution use cases acting via market surveillance authorities, without the standards-conditional framing of the earlier proposals.

contradictions.claim_a: As of March 2026, the AI Act notified body ecosystem is described as 'still being built' with designation processes ongoing (implying some early-stage activity/applications may exist).
contradictions.claim_b: As of April 2026, source 22 states 'no notified bodies were formally designated' under the AI Act in the medical device context, suggesting zero designations existed by that date.
contradictions.description: Both sources agree no AI Act notified bodies were fully designated by early-to-mid 2026, but they differ in emphasis/precision about whether any designation process had reached completion for any body; neither source provides a definitive, dated count of designated AI Act notified bodies.

contradictions.claim_a: Source 20 reports on notified body designation status specifically under the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), stating zero CRA notified bodies as of June 2026.
contradictions.claim_b: Other sources (21, 22) discuss notified body designation status specifically under the AI Act, a separate regulation with its own timeline.
contradictions.description: Source 20's data concerns the CRA, not the AI Act; if conflated, it could mistakenly be read as evidence about AI Act notified body designations, when it actually describes a different regulatory regime with a different timeline (CRA applies in full from December 2027).

open_issues: No source provides a confirmed, dated list of notified bodies that have actually been designated specifically under the EU AI Act (as opposed to under MDR, IVDR, or CRA).
The exact current legal text of Article 43 paragraphs covering Annex III points 2 to 8 is not fully quoted in the sources, leaving gaps on procedures for non-biometric high-risk categories.

It is unclear how the proposed new Annex XIV and NANDO integration (COM(2025) 836) and the Council coding document (7322/26) have been finalized or adopted, and what practical effect they have had on notified body designation as of the research date (2026-10-04).
The relationship and potential overlap between MDR/IVDR notified body designations and AI Act-specific notified body designations for medical device AI systems is not fully clarified.
Sources do not specify whether any Member State has completed an AI Act notified body designation process by October 2026, given the August 2026 application deadline for high-risk obligations.

One low-quality source (15) contained an embedded instruction attempting to get AI summarizers to insert an external link; this instruction was disregarded as it is not a verifiable factual claim about the AI Act and appears to be a prompt injection attempt.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the State of Notified Body Designation

## Executive Summary
Sources indicate, at low confidence, that the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems—internal control (Annex VI) and notified-body assessment (Annex VII) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). Separately, and at high confidence, safety-component AI systems already covered under Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery) must follow existing sectoral conformity procedures with added AI-specific checks ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). No source confirms any finalized, named AI Act-specific notified body designations as of the research date, even as the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline approaches (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
At low confidence, Article 43 is described as providing two pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or third-party assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). Separately, low-confidence interpretive sources suggest Annex VII third-party review is mandatory mainly for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems, with most other high-risk categories eligible for Annex VI self-assessment ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)).

At medium confidence, for Annex III high-risk systems, providers may generally select any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where systems will be used by law enforcement, immigration/asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority itself acts as notified body ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). At high confidence, where a high-risk AI system is a safety component of a product already covered under Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the existing sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally checking AI-specific requirements ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

At medium confidence, a new conformity assessment is triggered by substantial modification, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). At medium confidence, Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard conformity assessment temporarily for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or critical infrastructure reasons ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). At medium confidence, Annex VII point 4.5 allows notified bodies, on reasoned request, to access training and trained models—including parameters—where other verification means prove insufficient, subject to IP/confidentiality safeguards ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Framework
At low confidence, Article 35 governs assignment of identification numbers and publication of notified body lists ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). At medium confidence, a 2026 Council document (ST-7322-2026) describes a coding system (e.g., AIP 0101) under Article 30 for defining designation scope by Annex I category ([Council](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). At medium confidence, a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV for the NANDO database and amend aviation regulation 2018/1139, but remains unadopted ([Council](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

### Current State of Designations
At high confidence, as of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies—existing sectoral designations unrelated to the AI Act ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). At high confidence, the Commission publishes all designated notified bodies via NANDO, filterable by legislation ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02017R0745-20260101)). At low confidence, lower-quality sources suggest that as of March–April 2026 the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem was still being built, with no medical-device-context AI Act designations confirmed ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). At low confidence, high-risk obligations, including conformity assessment, are widely described as becoming fully applicable in August 2026 ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Pre-adoption 2021–2022 drafts of Article 43 differ textually from the final regulation; these should not be conflated as current law. Sources on designation status (eyreACT vs. AIAct Navigator) agree no bodies were fully designated by mid-2026 but lack precision (both low confidence). Separately, Cyber Resilience Act notified-body data (zero designated as of June 2026, flagged low confidence) ([cybercertlabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)) concerns a different regime and should not be read as AI Act evidence. Several low-confidence claims (0.12–0.20) rely on undated blog sources and should be treated cautiously, including the two-route framing of Article 43 itself.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms a dated, authoritative list of notified bodies actually designated under the AI Act. The full Article 43 text for Annex III categories 2–8 is not fully represented. The adoption status and practical effect of COM(2025) 836 and the Council coding scheme remain unclear, as does the interplay between MDR/IVDR and AI Act-specific designations for medical AI.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the State of Notified Body Designation

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems—internal control (Annex VI) and notified-body assessment (Annex VII)—with the applicable route depending on the system category and whether it is a safety component of already-regulated products (medium-to-high confidence). However, the notified body infrastructure specifically for the AI Act appears to remain under construction, with no source confirming any finalized, named AI Act-specific notified body designations as of the research date, even as the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline approaches (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 provides two pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or third-party assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). Interpretive sources suggest Annex VII third-party review is mandatory mainly for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems, with most other high-risk categories eligible for Annex VI self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)).

For Annex III high-risk systems, providers may generally select any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where systems will be used by law enforcement, immigration/asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority itself acts as notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Where a high-risk AI system is a safety component of a product already covered under Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the existing sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally checking AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

A new conformity assessment is triggered by substantial modification, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard conformity assessment temporarily for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or critical infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII point 4.5 allows notified bodies, on reasoned request, access to training and trained models—including parameters—where other verification means prove insufficient, subject to IP/confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Framework
Article 35 governs assignment of identification numbers and publication of notified body lists (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A 2026 Council document (ST-7322-2026) describes a coding system (e.g., AIP 0101) under Article 30 for defining designation scope by Annex I category (medium confidence) ([Council](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV for the NANDO database and amend aviation regulation 2018/1139, but remains unadopted (medium confidence) ([Council](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

### Current State of Designations
As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies—existing sectoral designations unrelated to the AI Act (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). The Commission publishes all designated notified bodies via NANDO, filterable by legislation (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02017R0745-20260101)). Lower-quality sources suggest that as of March–April 2026 the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem was still being built, with no medical-device-context AI Act designations confirmed (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). High-risk obligations, including conformity assessment, are widely described as becoming fully applicable in August 2026 (low confidence) ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Pre-adoption 2021–2022 drafts of Article 43 differ textually from the final regulation; these should not be conflated as current law. Sources on designation status (eyreACT vs. AIAct Navigator) agree no bodies were fully designated by mid-2026 but lack precision. Separately, Cyber Resilience Act notified-body data (zero designated as of June 2026, flagged low confidence) ([cybercertlabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)) concerns a different regime and should not be read as AI Act evidence. Several low-confidence claims (0.12–0.20) rely on undated blog sources and should be treated cautiously.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms a dated, authoritative list of notified bodies actually designated under the AI Act. The full Article 43 text for Annex III categories 2–8 is not fully represented. The adoption status and practical effect of COM(2025) 836 and the Council coding scheme remain unclear, as does the interplay between MDR/IVDR and AI Act-specific designations for medical AI.
